answer: EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD is read in the SMTP email backend's __init__ (django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:36). It sets self.password from settings.EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD when no password argument is passed. The default is an empty string "", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:203. The docstrings in django/core/mail/__init__.py (lines 71 and 100) also mention it.

SESSION_COOKIE_PATH defaults to "/" (defined in django/conf/global_settings.py). It is used in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py, in SessionMiddleware.process_response. It is passed as `path=` to response.delete_cookie (line 39) and to response.set_cookie (line 72).

SECURE_SSL_HOST is used in SecurityMiddleware (django/middleware/security.py), where __init__ reads it into self.redirect_host (line 16). process_request then uses it as the host in the HTTPS redirect (`host = self.redirect_host or request.get_host()`, line 28), but only when SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT is on. Its default is None, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py, so the redirect uses the request's own host.

LANGUAGE_COOKIE_DOMAIN is used in django/views/i18n.py (line 69) as the `domain=` argument when set_language sets the language cookie on the response. Its default, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py line 163, is None.

CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE is used in django/middleware/csrf.py:263, where it is passed as `secure=settings.CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE` when the CSRF cookie is set. It is also checked in django/core/checks/security/csrf.py (check_csrf_cookie_secure, line 40). Its default is False, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:568.

The core use is in ConnectionRouter.routers (django/db/utils.py), which falls back to settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS when no routers are passed, then imports any string entries and instantiates them. The default is an empty list, `DATABASE_ROUTERS = []`, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:184. The setting is also checked in model_checks.py, makemigrations.py, db/models/fields/related.py and test/signals.py.

STATICFILES_DIRS is used mainly in django/contrib/staticfiles/finders.py by FileSystemFinder (iterating settings.STATICFILES_DIRS to locate static files at line 61, and validating it in check() at lines 76-109). It is also referenced in django/core/checks/caches.py and django/test/signals.py. Its default is an empty list, `[]`, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py.

SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY defaults to True (defined in django/conf/global_settings.py). It is used when setting the session cookie in SessionMiddleware (django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:74, httponly=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY or None), and also in the cookie message storage (contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py:120) and the security check core/checks/security/sessions.py (check_session_cookie_httponly).

DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS is used in CommonMiddleware.process_request (django/middleware/common.py, line 43), which loops over settings.DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS and forbids requests whose User-Agent matches one of the regexes. Its default is an empty list [], defined in django/conf/global_settings.py line 245.

The default is True (defined in global_settings.py). It's read in django/conf/urls/i18n.py (line 13), django/utils/cache.py (lines 339 and 419), django/utils/translation/reloader.py (line 13), and most importantly django/utils/translation/__init__.py (line 65), where it chooses between trans_real and trans_null for the translation functions.

STATIC_ROOT defaults to None, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is used mainly in contrib/staticfiles/storage.py (StaticFilesStorage location = settings.STATIC_ROOT, line 26), and also in finders.py, utils.py, collectstatic, core/checks/caches.py, makemessages and test code.

EMAIL_USE_SSL is used in the SMTP email backend, django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py line 38, where `self.use_ssl = settings.EMAIL_USE_SSL if use_ssl is None else use_ssl`. Its default is False, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py line 205. Line 48 of smtp.py only mentions it in an error message about EMAIL_USE_TLS and EMAIL_USE_SSL being mutually exclusive.

The default is "django.contrib.sessions.backends.db" (defined in django/conf/global_settings.py). The setting is used via import_module(settings.SESSION_ENGINE) in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py (line 15, SessionMiddleware), the clearsessions management command (django/contrib/sessions/management/commands/clearsessions.py:14, 20), and the test client (django/test/client.py lines 741, 806, 822, 852, 867).

The setting is read in `_get_failure_view()` in django/middleware/csrf.py, which returns `get_callable(settings.CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW)` as the view used for CSRF rejections. The system check `check_csrf_failure_view` in django/core/checks/security/csrf.py also validates it. The default, set in global_settings.py, is "django.views.csrf.csrf_failure".

SESSION_COOKIE_AGE defaults to 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 2 = 1,209,600 seconds (two weeks), defined in global_settings.py. It is read in SessionBase.get_session_cookie_age() in django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py (returns settings.SESSION_COOKIE_AGE), which is used by get_expiry_age/get_expiry_date (base.py), the file backend (file.py:76) and the signed_cookies backend (max_age, signed_cookies.py:17).

The setting is read in FileSystemStorage.directory_permissions_mode (corpus/django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:64), which uses it as the fallback when no explicit directory_permissions_mode is given. It is also read in the in-memory storage (memory.py:208), and mixins.py:11 handles its change signal. Default is None, defined in corpus/django/conf/global_settings.py:333.

LANGUAGE_COOKIE_HTTPONLY is used in the set_language view in django/views/i18n.py. It is passed as httponly= to response.set_cookie() when the language cookie is set. Its default is False, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:166.

LOGGING_CONFIG is used in django.setup() (corpus/django/__init__.py:19), which calls configure_logging(settings.LOGGING_CONFIG, settings.LOGGING). configure_logging in django/utils/log.py (line 67) imports the callable with import_string and calls it with the LOGGING settings. Its default, in django/conf/global_settings.py, is "logging.config.dictConfig".

IGNORABLE_404_URLS is used in `BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware.is_ignorable_request` in django/middleware/common.py (line 178), which returns True if any pattern in `settings.IGNORABLE_404_URLS` matches the URI (`pattern.search(uri)`), so no 404 email is sent. Its default is an empty list, `[]`, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:259.

The default is "Lax", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. The setting is read in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py (SessionMiddleware.process_response). It is passed as samesite= to response.set_cookie when the session cookie is set (line 75) and to response.delete_cookie when it is deleted (line 41). It is also used in django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py (lines 121 and 127) for the messages cookie.

SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT is read in SecurityMiddleware.__init__ (django/middleware/security.py:15, `self.redirect = settings.SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`), which uses it to redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS. It is also checked by the security system check in django/core/checks/security/base.py:203. The default is False, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:667.

The default is "/accounts/login/", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. settings.LOGIN_URL is read as a fallback in: contrib/auth/decorators.py:25 (user_passes_test, which login_required and permission_required use), contrib/auth/mixins.py:25 (AccessMixin.get_login_url), contrib/auth/views.py:175 (logout_then_login), :183 (redirect_to_login) and :344 (the password reset context's login_url).

The default is "default" (global_settings.py:517). It is used in django/middleware/cache.py (lines 73 and 142, where the middleware sets self.cache_alias) and in django/utils/cache.py (lines 390 and 417, which look up caches[settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS]).

The default is TIME_ZONE = "America/Chicago", defined in global_settings.py. The setting is used in conf/__init__.py (lines ~208-217, where Settings sets os.environ["TZ"] and calls time.tzset()), in utils/timezone.py:52 (get_default_timezone), in db/backends/base/base.py (timezone_name / per-connection TIME_ZONE), and in test/signals.py (reacting to setting changes).

The default is None, defined in global_settings.py. The setting is used in: django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py (lines 40 and 71, when deleting and setting the session cookie), django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py (lines 118 and 126), django/middleware/csrf.py (line 321), and django/test/client.py (line 837, in the test client's session cookie).

MIGRATION_MODULES defaults to an empty dict ({}), defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is consumed mainly in MigrationLoader.migrations_module (django/db/migrations/loader.py:67-68), which returns the configured module for an app label. It is also used in db/backends/base/creation.py (lines 71-87, which temporarily overrides it while creating the test DB) and referenced in db/migrations/writer.py.

The default is 0, defined in global_settings.py. The setting is used in django/middleware/security.py (SecurityMiddleware.__init__ reads it as self.sts_seconds, to build the Strict-Transport-Security header) and in the security checks in django/core/checks/security/base.py (lines ~169, 177, 187).

The default is `STATIC_URL = None`, defined in django/conf/global_settings.py. It is used in many places. Settings.__setattr__/_add_script_prefix in django/conf/__init__.py:90 prefixes the script name onto relative values. Other uses: staticfiles storage (storage.py:28), staticfiles handlers (handlers.py:31), staticfiles urls (urls.py:13), staticfiles utils checks (utils.py:47), the `static` template tag (templatetags/static.py), the template context processor, the URL system checks (core/checks/urls.py:106), and test signals/testcases.

The setting is read in SecurityMiddleware.__init__ (django/middleware/security.py:19) and used in process_response to set the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header. It is also validated in django/core/checks/security/base.py (around lines 134 and 278). Default is "same-origin", defined in django/conf/global_settings.py.

The setting is used in SessionBase.get_expire_at_browser_close() in django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py (line 286). It is returned when the session has no custom "_session_expiry" value. It is defined in django/conf/global_settings.py:496 with a default of False.

The SMTP email backend (EmailBackend.__init__ in django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py) reads settings.EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD when no password argument is passed. The global default in django/conf/global_settings.py is an empty string "", so that is its value when a project doesn't set it.

The session middleware (SessionMiddleware.process_response in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py) reads SESSION_COOKIE_PATH. It uses it when it sets the session cookie (line 72) and when it deletes it (line 39). If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is "/".

SecurityMiddleware (django/middleware/security.py) reads SECURE_SSL_HOST in its __init__ and stores it as self.redirect_host. If a project doesn't set it, the default from global_settings.py is None. In that case process_request uses request.get_host() as the host for the HTTPS redirect.

The main reader is the ConnectionRouter class in django/db/utils.py. Its `routers` cached property falls back to settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS. Other places (system checks, makemigrations, related fields) also read it. The default, set in global_settings.py, is an empty list `[]`.

The `set_language` view in django/views/i18n.py reads LANGUAGE_COOKIE_DOMAIN. It passes the value as `domain=` when it sets the language cookie. If a project doesn't set it, the default from global_settings.py is `None`, so the cookie has no explicit domain.

The CSRF middleware (CsrfViewMiddleware._set_csrf_cookie in django/middleware/csrf.py) reads settings.CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE and passes it as `secure=` to response.set_cookie. The security system check check_csrf_cookie_secure in django/core/checks/security/csrf.py also reads it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is False, so the CSRF cookie is not marked Secure.

The staticfiles app's FileSystemFinder (django/contrib/staticfiles/finders.py) reads STATICFILES_DIRS. Its __init__ loops over it to build its locations, and its check() validates it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is an empty list ([]).

CommonMiddleware (django/middleware/common.py, process_request) reads settings.DISALLOWED_USER_AGENTS and raises PermissionDenied if a request's User-Agent matches any regex. The default in global_settings.py is an empty list [], so no user agents are blocked.

The session middleware (django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py, SessionMiddleware.process_response) reads it as httponly=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY or None when setting the session cookie. (The messages cookie storage and the security system check also read it.) If unset, it defaults to True, from django/conf/global_settings.py.

The SMTP email backend (EmailBackend.__init__ in django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py) reads settings.EMAIL_USE_SSL, when no use_ssl argument is passed. If the project doesn't set it, it takes the global default, False (global_settings.py:205).

Several parts read USE_I18N: the translation machinery (the `Trans` class in django/utils/translation/__init__.py, which picks trans_real vs trans_null), plus the i18n URL helpers, cache utils and the translation reloader. If a project doesn't set it, it takes the global default `True` (django/conf/global_settings.py:157).

The staticfiles app's StaticFilesStorage (django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py) reads STATIC_ROOT in its __init__ and uses it as the default storage `location`. The global default in django/conf/global_settings.py is `STATIC_ROOT = None`. With None, the storage sets location to None, and `path()` raises ImproperlyConfigured.

The CSRF middleware (django/middleware/csrf.py, `_get_failure_view()`) reads settings.CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW to pick the view for CSRF rejections. The system check in django/core/checks/security/csrf.py also reads it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from global_settings.py is "django.views.csrf.csrf_failure".

SessionMiddleware (django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:15) reads settings.SESSION_ENGINE and imports it with import_module. The clearsessions command and the test client read it the same way. If a project doesn't set it, the value is the default from global_settings, "django.contrib.sessions.backends.db", which is the database-backed session engine.

The session backends read it: SessionBase.get_session_cookie_age() in django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py returns settings.SESSION_COOKIE_AGE. When a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is 60*60*24*7*2 = 1209600 seconds (two weeks).

The file storage backends read it: FileSystemStorage.directory_permissions_mode (core/files/storage/filesystem.py) uses it as the fallback when no explicit directory_permissions_mode is passed. InMemoryStorage (memory.py:208) reads it the same way. If a project doesn't set it, the default from global_settings.py is None. That means no explicit chmod is applied to created directories, so the OS umask decides their permissions.

The `set_language` view in django/views/i18n.py reads it. It passes `settings.LANGUAGE_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` as `httponly=` to `response.set_cookie` when it sets the language cookie. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is `False`.

BrokenLinkEmailsMiddleware (django/middleware/common.py), in its is_ignorable_request method, reads settings.IGNORABLE_404_URLS. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is an empty list [].

The session middleware (SessionMiddleware.process_response in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py) reads SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE when it sets or deletes the session cookie. The messages CookieStorage (django/contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py) also reads it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is "Lax".

`django.setup()` reads `settings.LOGGING_CONFIG` and passes it, along with `settings.LOGGING`, to `django.utils.log.configure_logging`. `configure_logging` imports the dotted path and calls it on the logging settings. If a project doesn't set it, the default from `global_settings.py` is the string "logging.config.dictConfig".

SecurityMiddleware (django/middleware/security.py) reads SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT in __init__ and stores it as self.redirect. It uses that to redirect non-secure requests to HTTPS. If a project doesn't set it, it defaults to False (global_settings.py:667). The security system check in django/core/checks/security/base.py also reads it.

The django.contrib.auth code reads settings.LOGIN_URL: the login_required/user_passes_test decorators (auth/decorators.py:25), AccessMixin.get_login_url (auth/mixins.py:25), and auth views redirect_to_login/logout_then_login. When a project doesn't set it, the default from global_settings is "/accounts/login/".

Django's cache middleware reads it: UpdateCacheMiddleware.__init__ and FetchFromCacheMiddleware.__init__ in django/middleware/cache.py both set self.cache_alias from settings.CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS. The two helpers in django/utils/cache.py (lines 390 and 417) also read it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is "default".

The session middleware (SessionMiddleware.process_response in django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py) reads SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN to set or delete the session cookie's domain. Other readers are the messages cookie storage, the CSRF middleware and the test client. When a project doesn't set it, the value is None (the default in global_settings.py), so the cookie has no Domain attribute and is host-only.

Django's settings loader (the Settings class in django/conf/__init__.py) reads TIME_ZONE. It validates it against /usr/share/zoneinfo, exports it to os.environ["TZ"] and calls time.tzset(). django.utils.timezone (get_default_timezone) and the DB backends also read it. If a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is "America/Chicago".

The migration loader (MigrationLoader.migrations_module in django/db/migrations/loader.py) reads settings.MIGRATION_MODULES to find an app's migrations module. The test DB creation code (db/backends/base/creation.py) and the migration writer also touch it. When a project doesn't set it, the default from django/conf/global_settings.py is an empty dict {}, so the loader falls back to "<app package>.migrations".

SecurityMiddleware (django/middleware/security.py) reads settings.SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS into self.sts_seconds; the default when unset is 0 (global_settings.py: SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 0), so no HSTS header is sent. The security system checks also read it.

Several parts read it: the static template tag (templatetags/static.py), staticfiles storage (StaticFilesStorage), the staticfiles handler and urls, the context processor, and the system checks. The lazy settings object in conf/__init__.py prefixes the script prefix onto it only when it isn't None. When a project doesn't set it, STATIC_URL is None, which is the default in global_settings.py. Staticfiles code then raises ImproperlyConfigured through check_settings in staticfiles/utils.py.

The session backend base class (SessionBase.get_expire_at_browser_close in django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py) reads it, when the session has no "_session_expiry" value of its own. If the project doesn't set it, it is False, the default in django/conf/global_settings.py line 496.

SecurityMiddleware (django/middleware/security.py) reads settings.SECURE_CROSS_ORIGIN_OPENER_POLICY in __init__; if unset it defaults to "same-origin" (from django/conf/global_settings.py:660). The security system check in core/checks/security/base.py also reads it for validation.
